description: A working log for research taste: each row starts with a problem, names the prior art, makes a forecast, defines what would falsify it, and points to the cheapest next test.

items.problem: Reserve model serving for a future window with a right to reassign the entitlement. Touchmark already documents consented resale of unused contracts. The narrower opening is recovery of partially consumed commitments or enforceable throughput portability across providers.
items.why_now: Commercial and primary-source review completed 9 November 2026.
prior_art: Touchmark is direct. SF Compute operates resale of GPU hours with named customer cases. Architect launched a spot inference auction. Tuarā markets cross-provider matching, Tokexchange describes a closed credit pilot, and Corgi describes planned GPU resale.
items.forecast: Credible direct competition. Validate a narrower enterprise contract through a broker or host.
items.falsifier: Public quote requests and GPU resale demonstrate interest and adjacent usage. The price buyers will pay for inference transfer alone, resale fill rates, and delivered SLA performance remain unverified.
items.cheap_test: Quote identical reserved capacity with and without assignment, alongside a cancellation or rollover option. Collect a real payment for assignment and execute a transfer before building a venue.
items.result: Desk research only. No buyer interviews or paid tests.
items.belief_update: Two buyers choose and pay for transferability at a disclosed price

sources.title: Y Combinator company profile and launch
SF Compute named resale customer cases, September 28

items.problem: A converter commits to buy a specified grade of post-consumer resin, allowing a funding partner to advance against the contract and an independently verified lot. Document the actual cleanup and material flows separately.
items.why_now: Commercial and primary-source review completed 9 November 2026.
prior_art: The Body Shop confirms Indian recycled-plastic sourcing through Plastics For Change. The supplier offers physical resin, traceability and documented cleanups. Circulate Capital already finances Lucro, which has traceability and brand agreements.
items.forecast: Best near-term commercial test of the three. The potential opening is a specific underfinanced buyer-supplier lane, with repeated contracted delivery required.
items.falsifier: Third-country eligibility, grade consistency, rejects, freight, FX, payment delays and incumbent supply can erase margins. Visible cleanup does not establish how much saleable resin entered the lot.
items.cheap_test: Broker one non-food rigid HDPE lot through an existing recycler and buyer-approved certifier. Get a signed conditional purchase order and a financing quote before advancing funds.
items.result: Desk research only. No buyer interviews or paid tests.
items.belief_update: Buyer signs a PO specifying grade, acceptable origin evidence and rejection terms

sources.title: EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, Article 7
Plastics For Change supply and cleanup services
The Body Shop confirms sourcing from India
Circulate Capital follow-on investment in Lucro, July 2022

items.problem: Conditional commitments assemble a bundle of separately owned rights. Owners who accept receive a buyer-funded bonus if the required bundle fails to close. The market coordinates acquisition; it does not wager on an external event.
items.why_now: Research and competitor review completed 19 October 2026.
prior_art: Pieces describes bonder-funded refund bonuses for creator content; openmog terms describe sponsor-funded bonuses for sealed content. Product-level direct attempts in crowdfunding, with paid adoption and funding unverified. Anoma Public Signal is a concept; Allo implementations are experimental code. Land-assembly brokers already use options and conditional contracts.
items.forecast: Conditional opening. No scaled venue using this specific rights-assembly mechanism was established in the sources reviewed. This is a transaction-design hypothesis, not validated exchange demand.
items.falsifier: Laboratory coordination gains do not prove profitable real-world assembly. Existing options may solve enough of the problem. Unique holdouts, seller collusion, title defects and permitting remain; sponsor capital can be lost when assembly fails.
items.cheap_test: One buyer commits a capped bonus pool and a paid pilot
items.result: No customer interviews or paid pilots were conducted in this review.
items.belief_update: A buyer with a blocked, valuable bundle funds the bonus and pays a completion fee. Start with one asset class and measure incremental completed transactions against an option-based process.

items.problem: Sponsors commit to purchase qualifying outputs; researchers or suppliers compete to deliver. A further market could finance suppliers against enforceable purchase claims, but transferability and investor repayment must be established separately.
items.why_now: Research and competitor review completed 19 October 2026.
prior_art: Frontier has contracted carbon-removal purchases and published buyer fees. Wazoku/Innocentive and HeroX operate prize/solution marketplaces. Manifund has executed impact-certificate experiments, but its documentation restricts profits to charitable use. Hypercerts supplies records and funding infrastructure, not proof of liquid trading.
items.forecast: Commercial activity exists; broad greenfield thesis rejected. Conditional opening in pooled demand plus financeable claims for a specific underserved output. A general impact-token exchange is not supported by this review.
items.falsifier: Generic pay-for-results research is already served. A sponsor may change its mind unless the commitment is binding. Acceptance disputes, non-transferable claims, working-capital needs and IP terms can prevent investor financing.
items.cheap_test: At least two independent buyers sign the same output specification and purchasing terms
items.result: No customer interviews or paid pilots were conducted in this review.
items.belief_update: Find a specific shared deliverable that several buyers will pre-purchase on common acceptance and licensing terms. Secure sponsor commitments before recruiting speculative investors; prove one delivery and repeat purchase before a secondary venue.

items.problem: Prediction-market APIs are improving, but professional flow still lacks unified collateral, margin, custody, settlement, and cross-venue risk views.
items.why_now: Kalshi, Polymarket, ForecastEx, IBKR, PMXT, and venue aggregators are making the trading surface legible; the capital layer is now the bottleneck.
prior_art: Crypto followed the same path: CCXT unified APIs before FalconX, Hidden Road, and Coinbase Prime professionalized the capital layer.
Options became one market only after OCC-style clearing made contracts fungible across venues.
items.forecast: The first durable wedge is funded-account orchestration plus position, exposure, and resolution-risk monitoring, not full cross-venue clearing.
items.falsifier: Funds say venue-level accounts are fine, or the largest venues ship native portfolio margin and cross-venue reporting before independents gain trust.
items.cheap_test: Interview 10 prediction-market desks and ask what they reconcile daily by spreadsheet: balances, margin, resolution criteria, or venue limits.
items.belief_update: Strong until disproven by buyer calls.
items.public_artifact: Atlas opportunity note and target outreach list.

items.problem: CMBS analysis requires deal waterfalls, loan-level IRP data, property fundamentals, and market pricing, but the workflow remains expensive and specialist-heavy.
items.why_now: CRE stress and refinancing walls make loan-level collateral truth more valuable, while public EDGAR and trustee data are still messy enough to reward normalization.
prior_art: Trepp, CRED iQ, Bloomberg, KBRA, Moody's CRE, CoStar, MSCI-RCA, and Green Street cover pieces of the stack.
items.forecast: A narrow public-data teardown for one real deal can expose enough edge to support paid collateral surveillance memos.
items.falsifier: The free filings are too incomplete to produce useful property-level variance, or every useful field requires enterprise licenses.
items.cheap_test: Pick one recent public CMBS deal, parse the prospectus and one IRP file, then reconcile top-10 loan DSCR and occupancy against property-market comps.
items.belief_update: Worth one deal before any product build.

items.problem: Crypto execution is not one market: routers, AMMs, perp venues, prime brokers, custody networks, and data surfaces are different adapter shapes.
items.why_now: The atlas had only Talos in Crypto Infrastructure × L2, which hid the institutional execution and prime-brokerage layer.
prior_art: Talos and CoinRoutes are OEMS/SOR layers.
FalconX, Coinbase Prime, Hidden Road, Copper ClearLoop, and Fireblocks bridge execution with custody, financing, and settlement.
items.forecast: The best map is not a flat DEX list; it separates quote routers, pool protocols, perp venues, custody networks, and prime brokerage.
items.falsifier: Users cannot explain decisions better with adapter shapes than with ordinary company categories.
items.cheap_test: Use the updated matrix to classify 20 more crypto venues without adding any taxonomy keys.
items.result: Crypto-Native Infrastructure × L2 moved from 1 to 7 entries.
items.belief_update: Framework improved; still needs lending-rate adapters and router/pool coverage.

items.problem: Parcel, tax delinquency, title/lien, permits/code, crime, CMBS exposure, and local market comps are fragmented across public agencies and vendors.
items.why_now: Investors and operators want hyperlocal risk screens, but most products stop at parcel or listing data instead of area-level joined decision data.
prior_art: Reonomy, LightBox, Cherre, CompStak, CoStar, Crexi, and county assessor systems each cover fragments.
CMBS workflows prove the value of linking asset-level facts to financing structures.
items.forecast: The wedge is not another property database; it is county-level anomaly and diligence packs around distressed or financeable areas.
items.falsifier: County data quality and rights make automated joining too brittle outside a few pilot counties.
items.cheap_test: Build one county pack by hand for parcel + delinquency + liens + permits + crime around 50 properties and measure how many records reconcile cleanly.
items.belief_update: High friction, but good research artifact if scoped county-by-county.
